item.title: Isuzu Florian TS (1969)
item.description:
Publication: Car Graphic
Format: Road Impression
Date: September 1969
Author: Kenji Kikuchi

Road-testing the Isuzu Florian TS

There are no outstanding features or attention-grabbing qualities to speak of, but the Florian TS (Touring Sports, PA20SD) is a sporting sedan built with thoughtful attention to detail and a conscientious approach. It was introduced this past March, when the Florian series underwent a minor change, as a model positioned between the existing Deluxe and Super Deluxe. Its character is much the same as that of the Bellett 1600 Sports, but it is a new model aimed at a market one class higher.

item.title: Isuzu Florian 1800 Touring Deluxe (1971)
item.description:
Publication: Motor Fan
Format: Test Drive Report
Date: January 1971
Author: Shuzo Araki

Flexible Engine, Supple Ride

A quiet, spacious interior. Light, effortless controls. Already a pure family sedan, the Florian, has gained a new 1800cc engine that further strengthens its character.

The Advantages of Greater Displacement

Increasing engine displacement while leaving the body unchanged is a well-established approach. Indeed, it is no exaggeration to say that nearly every Japanese car has followed this path. In the so-called “popular car” class, the familiar progression has been to begin at 800cc, then grow to 1000cc, 1200cc, and 1300cc. Meanwhile, some engines originally introduced at 1300cc have ultimately been enlarged to displacements as high as 1800cc.
